correctness.rationale: The computation is correct as a reduced result, not a raw scheme assertion. In a nonzero triple product xyz, multiplication of a proposed relation among x,y,z,xy,xz,yz,xyz first by yz,xz,xy and then by z,y,x isolates all coefficients using commutativity, associativity and zero squares. Thus dimension three forces A³=0. Nonzero image lies in the annihilator, and annihilator codimension must be at least two for a nonzero alternating form on the quotient. The annihilator and image are therefore the same line Kw. The space of alternating forms on the two-dimensional quotient is one-dimensional, generated by det(w,−,−). This gives cwwᵀ in the stated mixed-product ordering (the cyclic signs are positive in characteristic two). Conversely any rank-one symmetric matrix over a field has this form by proportionality of the row and column lines, without needing c to be a square; the annihilator then contains the image. The minor relations on symmetric coordinates generate the prime kernel of the Veronese map by swapping partners of the same index multiset. Its degree-m dimension is binom(2m+2,2); summation gives the stated series, dimension and degree. Some diagonal entry is nonzero at every nonzero geometric point, giving smooth charts via the elementary minor equations, while all six tangent coordinates survive at zero. Over F_q there are q−1 distinct nonzero laws per image line, hence q³ total including zero. The frozen finite-field checker was inspected, not executed, and is not needed in place of the all-field argument.

originality.rationale: The asserted new geometry and count follow mechanically from the explicitly credited normal form and the basis-change law. This is not a priority verdict based on exact wording, a same-day hit, or source access. The frozen record credits the zero law and single nonzero associative class. The nonzero class is represented by e₂e₃=e₁ only, since that law is nonzero, square-zero and associative. In precisely the frozen matrix convention, Λ²V≅V*⊗det(V), so transport of that law by g takes E₁₁ to (det g)⁻¹(g e₁)(g e₁)ᵀ. Conversely, complete any nonzero w to a basis and scale a second column to set det g=c⁻¹; this realizes every cwwᵀ over the ground field, including nonperfect fields. Thus the prior normal-form classification in these coordinates directly gives the rank-one symmetric orbit, not merely its abstract orbit type. Over the algebraic closure its reduced closure (adding zero) is the standard second Veronese cone by the monomial map; its minors, Hilbert series, dimension, degree and vertex singularity are the usual invariants of that cone. The finite-field census is likewise the immediate count of one nonzero scalar per allowed parameter c for each fixed w on each image line, namely (q−1) per line. The early Jordan classification excludes F₂; the broader zeropotent classification has arbitrary-field scope. Even apart from that source comparison, F₂ just specializes the same orbit calculation and can be handled with the three-dimensional annihilator argument; it does not establish a distinct new geometric or enumerative stratum.
residual_risks: The original detailed classification passages were not independently retrieved; the rejection rests on the explicit prior normal-form credit and reconstructed implication, not a claim to have seen an earlier paper print the Veronese ideal or census.
